metadata.tool: tools/db/shadowed_migration_replay.py (mvs-audit-03-d2, with the d3 baseline-pinning fix)
metadata.command: python tools/db/shadowed_migration_replay.py --json --baseline-db <path outside the repo> --migration <each of the 40>

baseline.note: remaining_failures are migrations SQLite cannot apply (mostly PostgreSQL-only DDL). Objects they would create are absent from this baseline, so a gap verdict resting on such an object is weak.

oracles: 1. SQLite replay - every migration the runner actually applies, then the shadowed entry against a throwaway copy, diffing normalised sqlite_master DDL.
2. Live PostgreSQL - information_schema.tables/columns + pg_indexes + pg_constraint on the local icdev database, read-only session.

3. tools/db/schema/pg_consolidated.sql - what bootstrap_pg.py loads on a FRESH PostgreSQL database. through_version=301 means every migration at or below 301 is marked applied WITHOUT running, so an object absent here is absent from a new deployment for good. This is the oracle that decides.
4. Declaring-source scan - CREATE TABLE/INDEX across tools/ and apps/ outside the migration trees, to find canvases and reflexes that create their tables at app startup.
metadata.why_oracle_3_decides: tools/db/init_icdev_db.py, which declares several of these objects, refuses to run when ICDEV_STORAGE_BACKEND=postgresql. A fresh PostgreSQL database therefore gets its schema from pg_consolidated.sql plus migrations above through_version, and from nowhere else.
